findings.text: the command writes through the head-less selection (newest record) while reckon/crew/recovery.py:select_review_for_head reads back the first candidate carrying the head, so a store holding both the legacy and the revision-keyed record for one head answers ok: true and leaves the sub-floor row standing — reproduced with a live pointer in review-reproduction.log, where shapes B and C report exit=0 with the disposition present only in the .at- file and the durability row still listed, against shape A which clears it; the store on this workstation holds that shape for 343 of its 570 runs, and r-20260928T180802952100 already carries an exempted durability disposition in its .at- file alone, which the reader that reports the row does not see.

plots the base arm as "0 passed, 8 failed" and the fragment's alt text repeats that reading, while arms/baseline_suite.log reads "8 failed, 40 passed" and the fragment's own table three lines above says the same — a reader of the figure or of the alt text alone is told the base gate was 8 cases, not the 48 the other two arms are measured over, so the population the change is compared against is misstated.

a --reason supplied with --kind folded, or a --node supplied with --kind exempted, is accepted and silently dropped: reckon/cli.py:3847 hands both to a writer whose predicate reads only the one its kind needs, so the operator's text is discarded while the receipt still reads ok: true.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; 857e514c adds the subcommand, the ten cases and the two documents, and 96ab817c replaces the writer's second copy of the closed set with dimension_disposition_valid and corrects the floor-of-zero comment at reckon/crew/review.py:1166.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when's measure is tests/test_sub_floor_disposition_has_a_writer.py, whose ten cases assert the row's return through the obligations read-back after driving the CLI; its arms are logged at arms/baseline_suite.log (8 failed, 40 passed, EXIT=1 at 5636e306, the failures exactly the new module's command cases) and arms/after_suite.log (48 passed, EXIT=0), and I reproduced the head arm independently at 96ab817c.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a coordinator retires a sub-floor review dimension through a crew command instead of editing the review store by hand; reckon/cli.py:3793 adds `crew dispose` and reckon/crew/review.py:1329 makes the writer's gate the reader's own predicate, and the command retires the row on a store holding only the revision-keyed record — but where the store also holds the legacy record for the same head it exits ok: true and the row stands, which is the shape 343 of the 570 runs in ~/.config/reckon/crew/reviews/reckon already have.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; its commits, changed_paths, test_logs, baseline_suite and after_suite records and the bare negative_control_log path all match the logs and the diff, and the commits it names are the commits the fragment's evidence anchor cites.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node was fenced to reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/review.py, tests/test_sub_floor_disposition_has_a_writer.py, the fragment and the figure directory; `git diff --stat 5636e306 96ab817c` lists six files and every one is inside that fence.

justifications.durability: removing the kind check from dimension_disposition_valid reddens exactly the two unknown-kind cases and the refusals are asserted through the obligations read-back rather than the command's own receipt, but no case builds a store holding both records, so nothing fails if the write-path divergence regresses.
justifications.evidence: the gate measures what the done-when asserts and each arm ends in an EXIT= line (arms/after_suite.log 48 passed EXIT=0, arms/baseline_suite.log 8 failed 40 passed EXIT=1), but the delivered figure and its alt text misstate the base arm against that log.
justifications.fit: making the writer's gate the reader's own predicate at reckon/crew/review.py:1329 matches the module's idiom and the refusing refusals reuse the store's own messages, though the write-back-path claim at reckon/cli.py:3840 and reckon/crew/review.py:1314 is not what the code does when the newest record is not the one a head-named reader selects.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/cli.py:3847 records the disposition through a head-less selection (the newest record) while the obligation row is read back by a head-named one, so on the dual-record store the goal's retire-by-command does not happen and the coordinator is back to hand-editing, as review-reproduction.log shapes B and C show.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --stat 5636e306 96ab817c` touches exactly the six files under the five declared write paths, and the review.py comment correction is the one the goal names.
